analysis.implementation_strategy: Extend core/capability_bridge.py + core/net_ports.py to classify every capability's storage via datastore ports; enforce Postgres RLS/object-store rules via config/agent-capability-vector.json, capability-packs.json, and data-plane-threats.json lint rules. No new component; default port adapters wrap Postgres + S3-compatible store.
conflict_findings: BI-PF-0414 may add non-Postgres stores concurrently in net_ports adapters
BI-0043 pipeline file-store truths could be read as bypassing the standard
duplication_findings: BI-PF-1292 defines EDP itself - this item only sets/enforce the standard on top
BI-PF-0414 pluggable SQLite store is an allowed test/dev exception to document, not duplicate work
BI-0043 hybrid file-store stance conflicts at wording level only
analysis.rationale: Standard enforcement is best served by extending existing capability-bridge/net_ports plumbing and config vectors; new component would duplicate EDP epic work. Low drift, clear deps on BI-PF-1292.
assumptions: Datastore port abstraction already exists via net_ports/capability_bridge
BI-PF-1292 provides Postgres RLS and object-store adapters as primitives
Standard applies to new and migrated capabilities, not one-off spikes
risks: Enforcement could block dev/test flows needing SQLite or local files
Existing capabilities may lack declared storage ports (undocumented bespoke stores)
Over-broad standard could stall delivery of thin spikes
evidence: Reuse of candidate files limits surface area
Low drift vs settled EDP epic
Dependencies clearly map to existing backlog
missing_info: Which capabilities are exempt (spikes, CI/local dev)?
Is SQLite allowed as dev-only default per BI-PF-0414 or prohibited entirely?
Enforcement mechanism: build-time lint, runtime assert, or both?

context_review.reason: Title/policy text copied verbatim into every field; no concrete capabilities to migrate, no listed files/components, no actionable migration steps or verification beyond restating the standard.
